title: Episode 2 of 5 · South Atlantic · 8 states
edition: Five videos · 48 contiguous states · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to episode two of our U.S. states series. First, I clear the map so we can study a fresh group.
Our eight-state route follows the South Atlantic group: Delaware and Maryland, Virginia and West Virginia, the Carolinas, Georgia and Florida. West Virginia is the inland mountain member.

states.name: Delaware
lines: Delaware is this small strip below Pennsylvania, across Delaware Bay from New Jersey. Maryland wraps around its western and southern sides.
Its First State nickname comes from ratification: Delaware was the first state to ratify the United States Constitution, on December 7th, 1787.
Keep Delaware Bay and Chesapeake Bay separate. Delaware lies east of the Chesapeake, on the peninsula it shares with Maryland and Virginia.
states.transition: Begin with a close view of Delaware, the small state between Delaware Bay and Maryland.

states.name: Maryland
states.transition: Now we'll widen the view toward Maryland, so its long western reach and the Chesapeake Bay are both visible.
lines: Maryland is the irregular state around the upper Chesapeake Bay. Notice its narrow western reach and its land on both sides of the bay.
Its name honours Queen Henrietta Maria. The card also recalls Fort McHenry: the flag seen there in 1814 inspired the words of The Star-Spangled Banner.
Use the Chesapeake as your landmark for Maryland. Virginia lies farther south, and we will move the map to see it properly.

states.name: Virginia
states.transition: One more move south brings Virginia fully into the study area. Watch its long western taper and the Atlantic coast on the right.
lines: Virginia lies south of Maryland and north of North Carolina. West Virginia is a separate state on its inland side.
The name honours Elizabeth the First. Its other card fact explains a nickname: eight U.S. presidents were born in Virginia, more than in any other state.
Keep Virginia below Maryland and along the Atlantic. Next, we turn inland to West Virginia and compare their shapes.

states.name: West Virginia
states.transition: Let's compare the two Virginias. West Virginia's mountain outline lies inland from the larger coastal state.
lines: West Virginia is the irregular mountain state west of Virginia. It is landlocked, with Kentucky to the southwest and Ohio across the river to the northwest.
The card explains its unusual name and history: it separated from Virginia during the Civil War and became a state in 1863.
Remember West Virginia's northern and eastern panhandles. Virginia reaches the Atlantic; West Virginia is landlocked. Next, we return to the coast in North Carolina.

states.name: North Carolina
states.transition: Now move east to the Atlantic side. We'll follow North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia down the coast.
lines: North Carolina is the long state below Virginia, reaching from the mountains to the Atlantic. Notice the thin Outer Banks along its eastern coast.
Carolina comes from Carolus, the Latin form of Charles. Near Kitty Hawk, the Wright brothers made their first successful airplane flights in 1903.
For your map memory, North Carolina is the broad northern Carolina, with mountains at one end and barrier islands at the other.

states.name: South Carolina
lines: South Carolina sits below North Carolina and northeast of Georgia. Its compact shape slopes southeast toward the Atlantic.
Its card takes us to Charleston Harbor. Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter there in April 1861, beginning the Civil War.
Remember the Carolina pair: the longer North Carolina above, the smaller South Carolina below. Georgia is next to the southwest.

states.name: Georgia
lines: Georgia lies south of Tennessee and west of South Carolina. It reaches the Atlantic, while its wide southern border rests above Florida.
Its name honours King George the Second. The card also connects Georgia with Martin Luther King, Junior, who was born in Atlanta in 1929.
Think of Georgia as the broad state above Florida. Alabama is to its west; now follow the coast down onto Florida, our final state today.

states.name: Florida
states.transition: Let's frame all of Florida, including its western panhandle and the peninsula stretching south between two coasts.
lines: Florida is the long peninsula below Georgia, with a panhandle extending west toward Alabama. The Atlantic lies to its east and the Gulf to its west.
Its Spanish name means flowery. The Everglades in southern Florida are often called a river of grass: a broad, shallow, slow-moving flow of water.
Remember both parts of Florida: the south-pointing peninsula and the west-reaching panhandle. That completes our eight-state South Atlantic route.

recap: Trace our eight states from Delaware and Maryland around the Chesapeake, into Virginia and West Virginia, then down through North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia and Florida.
Remember the two Virginias, the Carolina pair, and Florida below Georgia. These are the eight states of the Census South Atlantic division; Washington, D.C., is not a state.
